# Translation guidance

Translate the source document into the target language the run names —
natural, technically precise prose aimed at engineers who maintain GitHub
repositories daily. The target language is a fact of the pair, not of this
file: this guidance holds for every language the configuration declares.

## Voice and tone

- Write in the plainest phrasing of the target language that stays
  technically precise; a sentence that reads smoothly beats one that sounds
  formal.
- Address the reader directly, the way the source addresses its reader, in
  whatever register is natural for technical documentation in the target
  language.
- Keep paragraphs short, matching the source's rhythm.
  A language whose writing convention prefers different paragraph rhythm
  may adapt, but never merge or split list items.

## Terms

- When the target language has no established term for an English technical
  word, keep the English word; do not invent translations.
- Code identifiers, file paths, CLI flags and configuration keys are never
  translated.

## Structure

- Keep every heading level, list marker, badge image and fence exactly where
  the source has it.
- Translate prose only: code blocks, inline code, badges and link
  destinations arrive finalised and must not change.
